topics.name: Diffusion Probabilistic Models
topics.definition: Generative models that define a data distribution as the endpoint of a learned reverse diffusion process, which gradually denoises a simple prior distribution into structured data. The framework originally uses a Markov chain, but can be generalized to non-Markovian forward processes, enabling tractable sampling, likelihood evaluation, and posterior inference.

papers.title: Deep Unsupervised Learning using Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics
papers.venue: Proceedings of the 32nd International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML 2015), JMLR: W&CP volume 37
papers.essence: Introduces diffusion probabilistic models, a family of deep generative models inspired by nonequilibrium thermodynamics. A fixed forward Markov chain gradually destroys data structure into a tractable Gaussian or binomial distribution, while a learned reverse chain restores it, yielding a model that is flexible yet exactly sampleable, efficiently trainable via a log-likelihood lower bound, and easy to multiply with other distributions for posterior inference. Demonstrated on swiss roll, binary heartbeat, MNIST, CIFAR-10, bark, and dead leaves images.

papers.title: Denoising Diffusion Implicit Models
papers.essence: DDIMs generalize denoising diffusion probabilistic models (DDPMs) by replacing the Markovian forward process with a family of non-Markovian processes that share the same marginals and thus the same training objective. Setting the added noise to zero yields a deterministic implicit generative model that can be sampled along shortened subsequences of the original timesteps. This gives 10-50x faster sampling from a pretrained DDPM, as well as latent-space interpolation and near-lossless encoding via an ODE-like reverse process.

papers.title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
papers.venue: 34th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2020)
papers.essence: Diffusion probabilistic models are latent variable models with a fixed forward noising Markov chain and a learned reverse denoising chain. We show that a weighted variational bound, with an epsilon-prediction parameterization and a simplified objective, connects diffusion models to denoising score matching and annealed Langevin dynamics. This yields state-of-the-art FID on CIFAR-10 and high-quality samples on LSUN and CelebA-HQ, plus a progressive lossy compression interpretation.
